summary.headline: Thomas Scott Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39% YoY to INR79 crore and PAT 34% to INR6 crore, with festive sales shifting out of the quarter.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 39% YoY to about INR79 crore, with EBITDA of about INR11 crore (13.31% margin, up 24% YoY) and PAT of about INR6 crore (7.98% margin, up 34%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 31% to INR145 crore and PAT rose 43% to about INR12 crore. Management said the quarter had no Dussehra sales because the cut-off was 30 September, so margins are not comparable YoY. The company also signed Forever 21 and Dockers licensing and global designated supplier agreements for South Asia and began targeting export revenue, to be reported separately from Q3.

financial_highlights.metric: Thomas Scott own brand revenue (Q2 FY27)
Licensed and other brands revenue (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: down from INR24 in FY24, about 25% lower

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR28 crore, up 28% YoY, driven by brand acceptance, online-first approach, rapid launches and higher push to online distributors and aggregators.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR49 crore, up about 52% YoY; H1 revenue INR87 crore, up 33%. Licensed portfolio is largely sold through Myntra and Flipkart.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR2 crore, down 29% YoY; H1 B2B revenue stable at INR6 crore. Management said domestic contract manufacturing has plateaued over the last 2-3 years.

segments.name: Export and global designated supplier (new)
segments.commentary: No revenue yet; export platform set up in Q2 and sales made in Q3, to be reported as a separate segment from coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management is not giving specific revenue guidance but targets high double-digit growth, similar to recent years.
Festive season (Dussehra and Diwali) responses reported as very encouraging; Q3 expected to capture festive sales that moved out of Q2.
Export revenue expected to be reported separately from Q3; management hopes to find a scalable operating model.
Related-party purchases from Bang Overseas about 70% of purchases currently, expected to fall to 30-40% in a year and to zero on the sales side from FY28.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 net capex about INR6.4 crore, mainly a large new warehouse in Gurgaon (partially operational, largest to date) and a warehouse in Bhiwandi, plus capacity extensions at Solapur.
Manufacturing footprint across Solapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.
Technology capex minimal; technology costs largely expensed.
Future infrastructure capex expected to be funded through term loans matched to asset life; working capital debt used as needed.
demand_pricing: Festive demand improved in Q2; Dussehra and Diwali responses since quarter-end described as very encouraging.
Own brand competes with online-first brands such as Snitch, The Souled Store, Bewakoof and Campus Sutra; international brands compete with Rare Rabbit and U.S. Polo Assn.
Marketing is brand-specific and not disclosed as a percentage of revenue; festive focus is on performance marketing and brand awareness on marketplaces.
Licensing of Forever 21 and Dockers for South Asia (India, Nepal, Bangladesh for Forever 21); management expects Dockers to lift margins and Forever 21 margins to be broadly similar.
Product mix H1 FY27: men's apparel 76%, women's 17%, women's accessories about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will export and licensing revenue be reported separately, and how do margins compare with pure export?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue not yet booked; a separate segment will be reported from Q3. Management expects at-par or better margins because inventory is shared with India and buyers can order from as few as 20-30 units per design, with no added India-type selling costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall in Q2 and other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Dussehra sales that fell in Q2 last year moved into October this year, so Q2 had no festive sales and margins are not comparable; some margin may shift into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did related-party purchases from Bang Overseas rise in FY26 to about INR116 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the share is falling as the company scales and adds other fabric suppliers at arm's length prices; the 6-monthly disclosure should show a significant decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 growth is base effect from last year's GST-related weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to separate base effect from underlying growth; growth targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to about 94 from about 124 in March; inventory days rose on INR20-30 crore of added finished and trade goods for festive and winter sales; payable days about 60.

qa_highlights.question: What is the related-party exposure and approval size?
qa_highlights.answer: Vedanta Creations is a wholly owned subsidiary of Bang Overseas. Purchases of fabric and garments are at arm's length. The INR100 crore approval was a blanket compliance approval, and future approvals will be rationalised.

risks_watch: Related-party purchases from Bang Overseas and Vedanta Creations, about 70% of purchases currently; the INR100 crore approval is large against a small turnover base.
Inventory days rising from INR20-30 crore of added stock; Q3 festive realisation needs to confirm.
Q2 EBITDA margin dip; Q3 must show whether festive sales offset it.
Export and Forever 21 and Dockers economics are unproven; no revenue yet and no disclosed margin or capex figures.
Management declined to give channel-wise margins, marketing spend percentage and FY27/FY28 revenue targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and new brand deals, but evasive on quantification: declined to split GST and festival base effects, channel margins, marketing percentage and revenue targets. Answers on related-party dealings were defensive and repeatedly stressed arm's-length pricing.
key_quotes: Our target right now is to set up the operational modus operandi largely for running this business.
Obviously, there should be a minimum overall order value, but at the design level, we are able to manage the inventory risk for our partners very well.
So, since the cut off is 30th September, there was not any Dussehra sale this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on high double-digit growth, new licences and export, but declined to quantify base effects, channel margins, marketing spend or revenue targets; analysts pressed on related-party purchases and margins, and answers were defensive on arm's-length pricing.

oneOffs.what: No Dussehra sales in Q2 FY27 because the cut-off moved to 30 September; festive sales shifted into October, so Q2 is not comparable and the timing shift depresses Q2 versus the prior year base

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew 39% to about INR79 crore, led by licensed brands (INR49 crore, +52%) and own brand (INR28 crore, +28%), with contract manufacturing down 29%; the brief does not quantify the Dussehra timing effect on revenue, and management said it is hard to separate the GST-related base effect from underlying growth, so the headline is only partly clean.
